doc_name: Russian annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts
text: On 30 September 2022, Russia unilaterally declared the annexation of areas in and around four Ukrainian oblasts—Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia, despite none of the oblasts being fully under Russian control at the time or since. The annexation followed internationally unrecognized referendums held from 23 to 27 September, organized by Russian occupation authorities in territories where hostilities were ongoing and much of the population had fled. The boundaries of the annexed areas were not defined, with Russian officials stating they would be determined later. The areas under Russian control at the time amounted to about 90,000 km² (15% of Ukraine’s territory, roughly the size of Portugal or Hungary), including about 60% of Donetsk Oblast, most of Luhansk Oblast, almost all of Kherson Oblast, and about 70% of Zaporizhzhia Oblast. Russia had previously occupied Crimea in 2014 and recognized the Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics in February 2022, launching a full-scale invasion on 23 February 2022, which included military occupations in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia. On 29 September, Russian authorities declared the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions independent as an intermediate step before annexation, and on 30 September, President Vladimir Putin signed accession treaties with the leaders of the four regions—Leonid Pasechnik, Denis Pushilin, Yevgeny Balitsky, and Volodymyr Saldo—while stating that the Donbas regions would maintain their 2014 borders and that other areas’ borders would be defined through consultations with residents. The annexation was condemned by the international community, including Ukraine, the European Union, the United States, and the United Nations, which rejected the referendums and the annexation as having no legal basis. The UN Security Council failed to pass a resolution condemning the annexation due to a Russian veto, and the UN General Assembly passed a resolution in October 2022 condemning the annexation and demanding Russia withdraw its forces. Only North Korea and formerly Ba'athist Syria recognized the annexation. On 19 October, Russia introduced martial law in the annexed areas, restricting public gatherings and personal liberties. The Ukrainian Kharkiv and Kherson counteroffensives enabled Ukraine to recapture parts of its territory, including Kherson on 11 November 2022. Russia’s State Duma and Federation Council unanimously approved the annexations, which were carried out in violation of Russian law. On 3 October, Putin stated that Donetsk and Luhansk would be annexed in their 2014 borders, while Kherson and Zaporizhzhia would have borders defined through consultations. A YouGov poll in February 2023 found that 63% of Swedes supported Ukraine in a war with Russia until Russian troops withdrew, and a Gallup poll in June 2023 showed that 62% of Americans supported Ukraine regaining lost territory, even if it prolonged the war. In response, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy declared that Ukraine would not negotiate with Russia as long as Putin was president and requested expedited NATO membership. A Kyiv International Institute of Sociology poll in May 2022 found that 82% of Ukrainians opposed any territorial concessions to Russia, and a September 2022 poll showed 87% opposed such concessions. Mykhailo Podolyak, an advisor to Zelenskyy, called the annexation a "Kremlin freak show" with no legal sense. In July 2024, a British Army official estimated that Russia would need five years and over 1.5 million casualties to fully control the annexed regions, with no winners in the conflict. In a 37-minute speech delivered on 30 September in the Grand Kremlin Palace, Putin justified the annexation as reflecting the "will of millions" of people, citing Article 1 of the UN Charter, while denouncing the West as totalitarian, despot, and Satanist, and accusing it of attempting to create a neo-colonial world order. Reuters noted that formal annexation would escalate the war and risk direct military confrontation with the United States and its allies. The Azerbaijani Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the referendums as "sham elections" on 9 September 2023.
